To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the augmenting response of the ventral posterior medial thalamus to layer V of the barrel cortex is initiated by pyramids and 2) the augmenting reponse is dynamically modulated by behavioral state in the awake, unrestrained animal.

the augmenting responses in the auditory thalamocortically pathway are initiated by the activation of layer V pyramidal neurons, that they can be modulated by behavioral state, and that their modulation is dependent on afferent activation of layer IV.
augmenting responses in the thalamocortically projecting pathway to layer V are initiated by pyramoidal cells in layer V and are dynamically modulated by behavioral state.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the augmenting response in the neocortical processing of sensory information.
the plasticity of thalamocortically projecting cells and its modulation by behavioral state.
the role of the thalamus and thalamocortically projecting cells in regulating the plasticity of the neocortex.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

augmenting responses in the thalamocortically evoked potentials in the rat somatosensory cortex are initiated by pyramdal cells in layer V of the cortex, that the responses can occur under both anesthetized and awake conditions, and that the responses can be dynamically modulated depending on the behavioral state of the animal.
the augmenting responses in the thalamocortically projecting cells are modulated by behavioral state.
the thalamocorticocortical pathway is a frequency-dependent pathway that is capable of short-term plastic changes that are dynamically modulated by the behavioral state of the animal.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

augmenting responses in thalamocortically projecting cells in layer V of the barrel cortex are modulated by behavioral state, with the strongest responses observed when animals are awake but immobile.
augmenting responses can be observed across behavioral states, are initiated in layer V of the neocortex, and have a frequency-dependent effect on the neostriatum.
thalamocortically projecting neurons are not just passive relays of sensory information to the cortex.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the thalamocortically driven activity of the neocortex is dynamically modulated by short-term plasticity, which can be triggered by the activity of the neoclortex itself.
the frequency-dependent properties of the thalamocortically projecting pathway can dynamically alter the neocortical response to sensory stimuli.
augmenting responses are a general property of thalamocortically projecting cells, and they can dynamically modulate their activity during natural behavior.
